sections.html:
Deltona is the largest municipality in Volusia County, sitting between Daytona Beach and Orlando, with an estimated population of 100,496. The city grew from a planned community of platted lots, so many houses share an age band, a floor plan and a lot size. Buyers line them up side by side, and that makes condition the biggest price driver. When repairs are what stands between you and a sale, an as-is cash purchase is often the simplest route.

The sections below cover utility accounts, the county tax calendar, what the state charges on a deed, and how homestead savings can move with you.

sections.h2: Closing out water and city accounts
sections.html:
Deltona owns its water and wastewater system. The city bought it from Florida Water Services on November 7, 2003, so you close the account with the city and not with a private company.

A short list keeps loose ends from lingering after the deed records:

  • Ask the city utility for a final meter reading on your closing date.
  • Hand the buyer the account details so service moves over without a gap.
  • Confirm that no code or permit matter is open on the property.
  • Update your mailing address with the Volusia County Property Appraiser so later mail finds you.

Ask Building and Zoning Services about permits that were never finished. Those can hold up a buyer's title work, and they are simpler to close out now than mid-contract.

sections.h2: Volusia County tax dates and discounts
sections.html:
Volusia's tax collector opens collection on November 1 and expects payment in full by March 31. Whatever is left on April 1 goes delinquent. A tax certificate sale on those delinquent accounts starts on or before June 1, and a local newspaper carries the list of accounts in the weeks beforehand.

If one lump sum is hard, ask about the installment plan: four payments, due June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31, with the application in before May 1. Homestead tax deferral requests are due by March 31. The Volusia County Tax Collector calendar has the current dates.

A sale during the year means the settlement statement splits that year's bill between you and the buyer. Have the title agent explain the division before closing day, not at the table.

The state's stamp tax on a deed runs 70 cents for each $100 of the price (section 201.02). Anyone named on the deed can be held responsible for it, even when the contract hands the bill to the other side. The clerk takes the money at filing.

  • Recording is billed separately under section 28.24: a set amount for page one, a smaller one for every page after, and a few add-ons.
  • Some transfers owe nothing, for instance an estate representative's deed issued under a probated will, or a homestead deed between spouses when a mortgage is the only consideration.

Find the clause that assigns these charges before you sign anything. Buyers who promise a fast closing can normally say in advance who covers the stamps and the title policy.

sections.h2: List, sell as-is or find a rehab buyer?
sections.html:
Sellers in town usually choose among three routes.

  1. Listing the house gets the most eyes, along with showings, an appraisal and whatever conditions a lender attaches.
  2. Selling as-is for cash removes the loan and most repair haggling.
  3. A renovation buyer fits a house with roof, plumbing or electrical problems that would make a lender balk.

If a mortgage is attached, get the payoff figure in writing. Then ask every buyer what you would actually net once all costs come out. Foreclosure papers already on file change the clock. After final judgment the clerk schedules the auction 20 to 35 days out, unless the plaintiff consents to more time.

sections.h2: City departments worth a call before you list
sections.html:
The city runs from a City Manager's Office through Enforcement Services, Public Works and Utilities, and Fire and Rescue. Three of its offices matter to a seller.

  • Building and Zoning Services can look up open permits at your address.
  • Enforcement Services handles code matters, so ask whether anything is pending against the lot.
  • Public Works and Utilities is where the water account lives.

Because so many Deltona homes were built in the same wave, buyers tend to compare roof age, air conditioner age and windows when they bid. Having dates and invoices for those items on hand helps you hold your price.

sections.h2: Taking homestead savings to your next home
sections.html:
Moving to another Florida home? Portability lets part of your Save Our Homes benefit follow you. Set up the new homestead inside three years of that January 1, then send Form DR-501T with Form DR-501 by March 1. The new home's assessed value is reduced by whichever is smaller: $500,000, or the difference between just value and assessed value on the old home.

An amendment from 2026 first reaches the 2027 tax roll. Call the Volusia County Property Appraiser to learn which rules govern your year.

A house's first homestead year is assessed at just value. Growth after that is limited each year to 3 percent or the CPI change, whichever is lower. The cap history stays behind when you sell, so anyone who has owned in Deltona a long time should speak with the appraiser before closing.

sections.h2: How a cash sale runs, start to finish
sections.html:
The sequence is plain, even when the house is not. First you describe the property candidly: condition, any tenant, any lender. A written offer comes back. On acceptance, a title company opens a file and hunts for liens, back taxes and open permits. Next come the contract and, at closing, a deed signed before two witnesses. The agent pays off loans, collects the stamp tax and recording charges, and hands you the balance. No inspection-driven repair list and no lender appraisal sit in that chain, which is why dates are easier to promise.

Before you accept, check the offer for the closing date, who pays costs and what happens to belongings left behind. Walk away from anyone asking for money from you before closing.

sections.h2: What to have ready for the title agent
sections.html: Most delays at closing come from missing paper. Gather your recorded deed, a lender payoff letter if you owe one, the newest tax bill and permit records for major repairs. Add the lease and deposit records when the house is rented. If an owner has died, expect the title company to ask who has authority to sign. Delivering all of this at the start lets the agent open the title search immediately, and the title search is what sets the speed of a cash sale.

faqs.q: Is Deltona the largest city in Volusia County?
faqs.a: Yes. Deltona is the largest municipality in Volusia County, with an estimated population of 100,496, and it sits between Daytona Beach and Orlando.

faqs.q: When did Deltona become a city?
faqs.a: December 31, 1995, after residents voted for incorporation that September. Earlier attempts in 1987 and 1990 failed.

faqs.q: Who closes my water account when I sell?
faqs.a: The city itself, which took over the water and wastewater system on November 7, 2003. Request a final reading dated to your closing.

faqs.q: By what date must a Volusia tax bill be paid in full?
faqs.a: March 31. After that the bill is delinquent on April 1, and the certificate sale opens by June 1.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Deltona house with a foreclosure pending?
faqs.a: Yes, provided closing happens ahead of the clerk's auction, which follows final judgment by 20 to 35 days barring the plaintiff's consent to longer. Contact a buyer and a title company as soon as you are served.
